info.title: data-box
info.description: Data and scraping behind one door: scrape, search, crawl, extract and run data sources (Firecrawl, Apify, Bright Data, Decodo and more), every paid call capped and metered. The same tools are served over MCP at /mcp.

get.summary: What works, what does not and why, and what recent calls cost
get.description:
What this box can do right now. Lists every provider (configured or not, and what it is for), the tools working now, any tool that is down with a one-line reason, spend over the last 24 hours, and the last 10 calls. Call it first when something fails, and report its reason instead of guessing.
Free; touches no provider.

post.summary: One public URL to markdown, text, HTML or links
post.description:
Read one public web page and return its content as markdown (default), plain text, raw HTML, or its list of links. Use it for any single URL you already have.
It runs the free direct fetch at once. Paid rungs never run without approval: when the free fetch is blocked, gets a challenge or a JavaScript-only page, the result says what stopped it (`blocked`) and carries a `plan` for the paid ladder (Firecrawl first; then Decodo, Bright Data, Firecrawl's browser, Hyperbrowser and browser-box as they are wired) with its worst-case cost. Show that plan to the user; on a yes, call execute with its plan_id and approve=true.
Do NOT use it to search or to walk a whole site (make a plan with kind search or crawl), or for private addresses: loopback, private, link-local and file targets are refused, on every redirect too.
Returns: content (or links), title, description, status_code, final_url, rung, rungs_tried, blocked and plan when the page was not the real page, job_id and cost_usd (always 0: the free rung).

post.summary: Get, list, cancel, page through or export a job
post.description:
Every call that can take a while is a job, and this is how you follow one.
get -> the job and its result (wait_seconds to wait for it to finish). list -> recent jobs (filter by status or tool). cancel -> stop it; paid steps already taken stay charged. results -> page through its items (offset, limit). export -> all items as csv, json or jsonl.
Free.

post.summary: Every source that could serve a need, tier by tier, and whether each can run (free)
post.description:
Step 2 of the four-step workflow on its own: survey every source that could serve a request, without planning or spending anything. Tier 1 is Firecrawl (its Alexandria providers, read live: price, page size, pagination, inputs, terms, field fit), MoltSets and DiscoLike; tier 2 Decodo and Bright Data; tier 3 Apify, the expensive backup's backup. Each source says whether it can run on this box and, if not, why.
Use it to answer "where could this data come from?". To get the data, call plan instead: it runs the same survey and turns it into a priced game plan.
Free.

post.summary: Steps 1-3: take a request, survey every source, return a priced game plan to approve
post.description:
Every paid pull starts here, whatever door it comes through. plan takes the request (step 1), surveys every source across the tiers and lists them all (step 2): for Firecrawl that means every tool in the Alexandria categories the request is about, read with its contract. Then it narrows them to a game plan (step 3): lanes ranked by records per credit x coverage x field fit, each proven by a preflight call (a lane whose preflight returns none of the entity is dropped and the next one tried), split into query x place cells and pages within the skill's caps, the dedupe keys, and the worst-case cost in credits and dollars against the live Firecrawl balance. A source the user named is honoured.
Nothing but the preflight is spent (at most 25 credits, and never more than max_cost_usd). The plan waits for approval and expires after 24 hours.
Then: SHOW THE WHOLE PLAN TO THE USER and wait for a yes. Only then call execute with its plan_id and approve=true. Never approve a plan on the user's behalf.
action=get returns a plan, action=list recent plans, action=cancel withdraws one (stopping its job).

post.summary: Step 4: run a plan the user approved, within its budget, resumably
post.description:
Runs a plan from `plan`, only after the user has approved it: pass its plan_id and approve=true. It spends at most the approved amount (the plan's budget, or a lower max_cost_usd), preflight included.
A pull runs its lanes in order (base layer first, then top-ups), stops a cell at its first short page or once its pages mostly repeat, stops calling once the deduped list reaches the requested count, never lets the Firecrawl balance go below zero, and dedupes across lanes on name+phone and name+address. Calling execute again on the same plan resumes it without paying for finished pages twice.
Returns counts, what each lane did, and a sample; the rows are read with job action=results or action=export (csv/json/jsonl). Records are deleted after the retention period (30 days).
drop_lanes leaves out lanes the user struck from the plan.
